text:
Maria Gomez: Quick follow-up to the control-plane separation RFC. I'm exploring a region-aware control-plane proxy model + ephemeral lease-based peering to the global control plane. Main idea: keep control traffic local by default, but establish short-lived peering tunnels to global CP for config syncs and rollouts. Thoughts? :thinking:

Aj Patel: curious — how do you envision auth for the ephemeral tunnels? short-lived certs? tokens?

Maria Gomez: short-lived certs issued by a central CA, rotated via a lease API. Lease model: proxy requests a lease, CA returns cert + expiration + allowed scopes. If lease expires, proxy falls back to local cached policy and marks region read-only until renewal.

Sanjay Rao: concern: what if a region loses connectivity to the CA? falling back to cached policy is ok for read, but rollouts requiring write will stop. How do we avoid silent divergence across regions?

Lee Chen: we could add a heartbeat escrow: when CP publishes a rollout it writes a small signed checkpoint into regional object store (S3-like) via the leased tunnel; proxies can pull checkpoints and verify signatures. That reduces need for live tunnel during rollout read.

Aj Patel: costs: per-region leased tunnels -> NAT/egress costs + extra BGP complexity if using direct peering. Also we need to consider private customers using VPC endpoints; some won't allow outbound peering to our relay hosts.

Maria Gomez: good point. For private deployments the agent will use an outbound reverse tunnel initiated from customer VPC to our regional ingress; lease handshake happens over that reverse tunnel so no inbound required. For dedicated customers with strict egress controls, we can support a relay pack you run in the DMZ.

Sanjay Rao: operational stuff: cert rotation is a big surface. We should ensure certs are short (5-15m) and use automated renewal with jitter to avoid stampedes. Also include a stale-policy TTL so proxies keep serving for a bounded window if renewal fails.

Maria Gomez: agreed. draft lease response shape (pseudo):
```json
{
  "cert_pem": "---BEGIN CERT---...",
  "expires_at": "2026-11-02T12:34:56Z",
  "scopes": ["config:read","rollout:ack"],
  "region": "us-west-2"
}
```

Lee Chen: fallback semantics: suggest 3-tier mode:
- normal: local proxy + fresh lease, full reads/writes
- degraded: lease expired but within stale-ttl, reads ok, writes blocked (queued)
- offline: stale-ttl expired, deny writes and emit metric + alert

Aj Patel: rollout plan? we need a canary that runs in 1 region + simulates CA outage for 10m to validate graceful degraded state. Also update our Console to show per-region lease health.

Maria Gomez: action items:
- Sanjay: spike automated cert churn + jitter (2w)
- Lee: add checkpoint pull + signed checkpoint proposal (1w)
- Aj: canary plan + console metrics fields (1w)
- I'll draft an RFC addendum describing lease API + response schema (3d)

agent-bot: @Maria Gomez created task: ARCH-1372 "lease-based region proxy spike" assigned to Sanjay, Lee, Aj.

Aj Patel: one more note — document egress/cost model for customers with per-tenant egress IP preservation. we should avoid forced SNAT changes during failover.

Maria Gomez: yes — incorporate egress-preservation patterns in the RFC addendum. thanks all :+1:
